hints.title: Consecutive Day Island Grouping
hints.text: Group consecutive calendar days of identical system states within 2019 into intervals of start and end dates.

hints.title: Gaps and Islands Row Number Difference
hints.text: Union failed and succeeded events for 2019. Subtract a contiguous row number from the event date to form invariant island keys.

hints.title: Contiguous Dates Blueprint
hints.text: with AllEvents as (select fail_date as dt, "failed" as state from Failed where fail_date between "2019-01-01" and "2019-12-31" union all select success_date as dt, "succeeded" as state from Succeeded where success_date between "2019-01-01" and "2019-12-31"), Ranked as (select state, dt, date_sub(dt, interval row_number() over (partition by state order by dt) day) as grp from AllEvents) select state as period_state, min(dt) as start_date, max(dt) as end_date from Ranked group by state, grp order by start_date asc.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH AllEvents AS (
    SELECT fail_date AS dt, 'failed' AS state
    FROM Failed
    WHERE fail_date BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-12-31'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT success_date AS dt, 'succeeded' AS state
    FROM Succeeded
    WHERE success_date BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-12-31'
),
Ranked AS (
    SELECT state, dt,
           DATE_SUB(dt, INTERVAL ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY dt) DAY) AS grp
    FROM AllEvents
)
SELECT state AS period_state,
       MIN(dt) AS start_date,
       MAX(dt) AS end_date
FROM Ranked
GROUP BY state, grp
ORDER BY start_date ASC;
```

variables: N: number of calendar event days in 2019
complexity.notes: Gaps and islands partition sorting by state and date executes in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking adjacent dates with recursive self-joins creates high combinatorial scanning overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The date minus row-number difference forms an invariant cluster key in a single window pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Classic gaps-and-islands pattern using DATE_SUB(dt, INTERVAL ROW_NUMBER() DAY).

WITH AllEvents AS (
    SELECT fail_date AS dt, 'failed' AS state
    FROM Failed
    WHERE fail_date BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-12-31'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT success_date AS dt, 'succeeded' AS state
    FROM Succeeded
    WHERE success_date BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-12-31'
),
Ranked AS (
    SELECT state, dt,
           dt - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY dt)) * INTERVAL '1 day' AS grp
    FROM AllEvents
)
SELECT state AS period_state,
       MIN(dt) AS start_date,
       MAX(dt) AS end_date
FROM Ranked
GROUP BY state, grp
ORDER BY start_date ASC;

import pandas as pd

def report_contiguous_dates(failed: pd.DataFrame, succeeded: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    f = failed[(failed['fail_date'] >= '2019-01-01') & (failed['fail_date'] <= '2019-12-31')].rename(columns={'fail_date': 'date'})
    f['state'] = 'failed'
    s = succeeded[(succeeded['success_date'] >= '2019-01-01') & (succeeded['success_date'] <= '2019-12-31')].rename(columns={'success_date': 'date'})
    s['state'] = 'succeeded'
    df = pd.concat([f, s]).sort_values(by='date').reset_index(drop=True)
    df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
    df['grp'] = (df['state'] != df['state'].shift(1)).cumsum()
    res = df.groupby(['grp', 'state']).agg(
        start_date=('date', 'min'),
        end_date=('date', 'max')
    ).reset_index()
    res['start_date'] = res['start_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    res['end_date'] = res['end_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    res.rename(columns={'state': 'period_state'}, inplace=True)
    return res.sort_values(by='start_date')[['period_state', 'start_date', 'end_date']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Consecutive State Shift Cumsum Grouping
